subject: Reasoning
question: Study the graph carefully and answer the question below. The bar graph shows the units of Laptops sold by A, B, C and D Companies in the two different months April and May. [Bar graph and data table showing units of laptops sold by 4 companies (A, B, C, D) in April and May. Y-axis: No. of laptops sold (0 to 1400 in steps of 200). For each company, two bars — April (left) and May (right). Data: A (April: 600, May: 1200), B (April: 1200, May: 960), C (April: 1000, May: 800), D (April: 400, May: 1000).] Laptops sold by Companies C and D together in May are more than laptops sold by Company B in April by what percent ?
explanation: The right pick is option B. C and D sold 800 + 1000 = 1800 laptops in May, while B sold 1200 in April; the excess is 600, which is 600 ÷ 1200 × 100 = 50% more. Percent-more items always need the smaller figure as the base.

subject: Reasoning
question: The distribution of land in a village under various food crops is represented by the pie-chart given below. Study the pie-chart carefully and answer the question no. 25 and 26. 25. If the yield per acre of rice is 50% more than that of wheat, then the production of wheat is what percent of that of rice ? [Pie chart: Rice 72°, Others 72°, Maize 99°, Bajra 45°, Jowar 18°, Barley 18°, Wheat 36°]
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Rice covers 72° and wheat 36° of the pie, so land under rice is twice that under wheat; with rice yield 50% higher per acre, rice production is three times wheat's, making wheat output one-third — 33⅓% — of rice. Pie angles give area shares; yield per acre converts area into production.

subject: Reasoning
question: A 60 litre mixture has color and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How much litre water should be added to make the ratio 3 : 5?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. In 60 L at 3 : 2 you have 36 L colour and 24 L water; to reach 3 : 5 the water must become 60 L while colour stays 36 L, so add 36 L of water. Ratio questions often reduce to holding one part fixed and solving for the other.

subject: Reasoning
question: 27. If a train with usual speed of 80 km/hr increases its speed to 100 km/hr, then reaches its destination 36 minutes earlier. Then how far is the destination ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The time saved is 36 minutes = 3/5 hour, and d/80 − d/100 = 3/5 gives d × (1/400) = 3/5, so distance d = 240 km. Same route, two speeds — set the time difference equal to the earlier minus the later journey time.

subject: Reasoning
question: 28. If two cars moving in the same direction with speed 80 km/hr and 70 km/hr, after how much time, both cars will be at a distance 60 km from each other ?
explanation: The right pick is option A. Relative speed in the same direction is 80 − 70 = 10 km/h, so to open a 60 km gap takes 60 ÷ 10 = 6 hours. Same-direction problems always use the speed difference, not the sum.

subject: Reasoning
question: The distribution of land in a village under various food crops is represented by the pie-chart given below. Study the pie-chart carefully and answer the question no. 25 and 26. 26. If the total area of food crop increased by 5% and the area under rice production increased by 12%, then what will be the angle for rice in the new pie-chart ? [Pie chart: Rice 72°, Others 72°, Maize 99°, Bajra 45°, Jowar 18°, Barley 18°, Wheat 36°]
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Total crop area rises 5% while rice area alone rises 12%, so rice's share becomes (1.12 ÷ 1.05) times its old share; 72° × 112/105 = 76.8° in the new pie. When only one slice grows faster than the whole, scale its old angle by the relative growth ratio.

subject: Reasoning
question: 29. The HCF and LCM of two numbers are respectively 24 and 168. Both the numbers are in the ratio 1 : 7. Find the greater of the two numbers.
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. With numbers in ratio 1 : 7, write them as x and 7x; HCF = x = 24, so the greater number is 7 × 24 = 168. Check: LCM of 24 and 168 is 168, matching the given data.

subject: Reasoning
question: 31. If a man bought 20 shares of Rs. 50 at Rs. 5 discount and the rate of dividend being 13 1/2%. Then the rate of interest obtained would be ________.
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Cost is 20 × (50 − 5) = ₹900 and dividend on face value is 13½% of ₹1000 = ₹135, giving return 135/900 × 100 = 15%. Dividend yield is always income divided by actual investment, not face value.

subject: Polity
question: 34. Which amongst the following Section of the Maharashtra Right to Public Service Act, 2015 deals with the powers and functions of the Maharashtra State Right to Service Commission ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Section 16 of the Maharashtra Right to Public Service Act, 2015 spells out the powers and functions of the Maharashtra State Right to Service Commission. Commission-related sections of this Act are high-yield for state-level exams.

subject: Reasoning
question: 30. 30% students read Sakal newspaper and 40% students read Lokmat newspaper, if 15% students read both newspapers, then what percentage of students do not read any newspaper ?
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Students reading at least one paper = 30 + 40 − 15 = 55%, so those reading neither = 100 − 55 = 45%. Inclusion–exclusion on a Venn diagram is the standard route for two-set overlap items.

subject: Polity
question: 33. Statement I : Under the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, 'Stipulated time limit' means the time limit as notified under Section 4. Statement II : The stipulated time limit may be extended by the State Government during the period of election. Choose the correct option :

options.A: Statement I is correct, statement II is incorrect
options.B: Statement II is correct, statement I is incorrect

explanation: The right pick is option B. Under the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, the State Government may extend stipulated time limits during elections (Statement II), but Statement I misstates how 'stipulated time limit' is defined in the Act. State-service Acts are frequent in Maharashtra-specific papers — read definitions in Section 2 carefully.

subject: Reasoning
question: 32. A wall of 100 meter can be built by 7 men or 10 women in 10 days. How many days will 14 men and 20 women take to built a wall of 600 meters ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Seven men finish 100 m in 10 days, so one man's daily output is 100/70 m; ten women do the same in 10 days, so one woman's rate is 100/100 = 1 m/day. Fourteen men plus twenty women deliver 40 m/day, hence 600 m needs 600 ÷ 40 = 15 days.

subject: Polity
question: 35. As per Section _________ of the Right to Information Act, 2005, every information of public authorities shall be disseminated widely and in such form and manner which is easily accessible to the public.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Section 4(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 requires every public authority to disseminate information widely in a form easily accessible to the public. Section 4 is the proactive-disclosure provision — do not confuse it with Section 6 (citizen requests).

subject: Polity
question: 36. Which of the following duties is not one of the Fundamental Duties included in the Indian Constitution ?

options.B: To promote harmony amongst the people of India,
options.D: To protect and improve the natural environment

explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Paying taxes promptly is a legal obligation under tax laws, not one of the eleven Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A. The listed duties cover the Constitution, harmony, environment, and national values — not tax payment.

subject: Polity
question: 39. Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the condition of socially and educationally backward classes in the territory of India ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and recommend remedial steps. Article 342 deals with specifying those classes, not appointing the inquiry commission.

subject: Polity
question: 38. Match the following. List I (a) Tenure of Vidhan Sabha (b) President of Gram Sabha (c) Tenure of Vidhan Parishad (d) Head of the Cabinet List II (i) Permanent Assembly (ii) Chief Minister (iii) 5 years (iv) Sarpanch
explanation: The right pick is option B. Vidhan Sabha serves a five-year term (iii), the Gram Sabha is chaired by the Sarpanch (iv), Vidhan Parishad is a continuing/permanent house (i), and the Cabinet is headed by the Chief Minister (ii) — giving iii, iv, i, ii. Panchayati Raj and state legislature basics often appear together in match-the-pair sets.

subject: Polity
question: 37. Which landmark judgement of Supreme Court of India introduced the concept of "creamy layer" within the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) ?

options.A: Indra Sawhney V. Union of India,
options.B: Ashok Kumar Thakur V. Union of India,
options.C: M. Nagraj V. Union of India,
options.D: Kesavanand Bharati V. State of Kerala

explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) introduced the 'creamy layer' concept to exclude affluent OBC members from reservation benefits. This nine-judge bench ruling remains the foundation of OBC quota jurisprudence.

subject: Polity
question: 40. Select the correct statements from the following. A. There shall be a High Court for each State. B. Every High Court shall be a Court of record and shall have all the powers of such Court including the power to punish for contempt of itself. C. Every High Court shall consists of a Chief Justice and such other Judges as the Governor may from time to time deem it necessary to appoint.
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Statements A and B reflect Articles 214 and 215 — each State has a High Court, and every High Court is a court of record with contempt powers. Statement C is wrong because High Court judges (other than the Chief Justice) are appointed by the President, not the Governor acting alone.

subject: Polity
question: 42. What are the qualifications for appointment as a Governor ? A. He must have completed the age of 35 years. B. He cannot be a member of either House of Parliament or State Legislature. C. He cannot be hold any other office of profit. D. He should be citizen of India.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Article 157–158 together require Indian citizenship, completion of 35 years, no membership of Parliament or any State legislature, and no holding of any other office of profit. All four conditions listed apply.

subject: Polity
question: 43. Select the correct statements from the following. A. The Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit. B. During any period, when the Vice-President acts as President or discharges the functions of the President under Article 65, he shall not perform the duties of the office of Chairman of the Council of States. C. During any period, when the Vice-President acts as a President, he shall be entitled to salary or allowance payable to the Chairman of the Council of States under Article 97.
explanation: The right pick is option A. The Vice-President is ex-officio Rajya Sabha Chairman and cannot hold another office of profit; when acting as President under Article 65, those Chairman duties stop. Statement (C) is wrong — in that period he draws the President's emoluments, not the Chairman's salary under Article 97.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following are exceptions to the rule of equality before law ? A. The President or the Governor is not answerable to any Court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office. B. The foreign sovereign, ambassadors and diplomats enjoy immunity from civil and criminal proceedings. C. The UNO and its agencies enjoy the diplomatic immunity.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Article 14's equality before law is qualified by well-known exceptions: presidential and gubernatorial immunity for official acts, diplomatic immunity for foreign sovereigns and envoys, and similar protection for the UN and its agencies. All three statements count.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is not related to Article 168 ?

options.A: For every State, there shall be a Legislature which shall consist of the Governor.
options.B: Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh States have two houses.
options.C: Where there are two Houses of the Legislature of the State, one shall be known as the Legislative Council and other as the Legislature Assembly.
options.D: Where there is only one House it shall be known as Legislative Council.

explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Article 168 defines how State Legislatures are constituted — with the Governor and one or two Houses. Where there is only one House, the Constitution names it the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council; that mislabelling is what breaks the Article 168 link.

subject: Polity
question: Who was the Chairman of the sub-committee formed to draft the Fundamental Rights provisions of the Constitution ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. J. B. Kripalani chaired the sub-committee of the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights that prepared the draft provisions on Fundamental Rights for the Constituent Assembly.

subject: Polity
question: Under Article 51, the State shall endeavour to A. Promote international peace and security B. Promote foreign policy and maintain international relations C. Maintain just and honourable relationships with other countries D. Encourage settlement of international disputes through arbitration
explanation: The right pick is option B. Article 51 (a Directive Principle) asks the State to foster international peace, maintain just and honourable relations among nations, and encourage arbitration for disputes — but it does not list 'promoting foreign policy' as a separate enumerated duty the way statement B suggests.

subject: Polity
question: In which of the following Article of the Constitution of India is the principle of collective responsibility of the State Council of Ministers enshrined ?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Article 164(2) expressly states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State — that is the constitutional home of collective responsibility at the State level.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the role of the Finance Commission of India in Centre-State relations ?

options.A: It advises the President on inter-state water disputes.
options.B: It allocates the borrowing powers of the States.
options.C: It recommends the distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States.
options.D: It supervises implementation of centrally sponsored schemes.

explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Under Articles 280 and related provisions, the Finance Commission's core job is to recommend how net proceeds of taxes should be shared between the Union and the States — it is not a water-disputes body, borrowing allocator, or scheme supervisor.

subject: Polity
question: 41. Which of the following statements is/are correct ? a. The Governor is the link between State and Centre. b. The Governor is the defacto head of State. c. There is a provision of Governor in Article 153. d. The Governor has the power to dissolve the Legislative Assembly prematurely.

options.A: Only statements a, b are correct
options.C: Only statements a, c and d are correct

explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. The Governor links the Centre and the State, is provided for in Article 153, and may dissolve the Assembly early in situations the Constitution allows — but the Chief Minister, not the Governor, is the real executive head of the State. Statement (b) is the trap; remember de jure versus de facto.

subject: History
question: Who is known as the first commentator on agriculture and farmer’s issues ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Jyotirao Phule's writings on agriculture, the plight of the peasantry, and rural exploitation — especially in works like Shetkaryaca Asud — earned him recognition as an early commentator on farmers' issues.

subject: History
question: Who propounded the theory that “Shudra Atishudra are the original inhabitants of India” ?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Mahatma Jyotirao Phule argued that Shudras and Ati-Shudras were the original inhabitants of India, overturning Brahmanical history that placed Aryan invaders at the centre of the narrative.

subject: History
question: Who founded the organization ‘Desi Trade Promotion Board’ in Pune ?
explanation: The right pick is option A. Ganesh Vasudeo Joshi ('Sarvajanik Kaka') founded the Desi Trade Promotion Board in Pune to encourage swadeshi commerce and strengthen indigenous trade during the nationalist period.

subject: History
question: The N. M. Joshi founded the __________ in 1911.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. N. M. Joshi established the Social Service League in Bombay in 1911 to carry out social welfare and labour-related uplift work — a stepping stone before his later leadership in the trade-union movement.

subject: History
question: What was the name of the educational plan discussed by Mahatma Gandhi through a series of articles published in the 'Harijan' newspaper in 1937 A.D. ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Gandhi outlined his basic education ideas through articles in Harijan in 1937, which became known as the Wardha Scheme — craft-centred, mother-tongue medium education discussed at the Wardha meeting.

subject: History
question: During the year 1817 - 18, which Raja of Nagpur fought against the British with the help of the tribal chiefs of Gond ?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Appasaheb Bhosale, the Bhonsle ruler of Nagpur, resisted the British during 1817–18 and drew support from Gond tribal chiefs — part of the final Anglo-Maratha conflict.

subject: History
question: Identify the person from the following description. i. He was a great patriot, thinker, writer and philosopher. ii. He established the Deccan Education Society and Fergusson College. iii. He started Anti-cow killing Samities, Akhadas and Lathi Clubs in Maharashtra. iv. His great contribution was that he taught the philosophy of defiance and guided to the people of India. a. Dadabhai Naoroji b. Gopal Krishna Gokhale c. Lokmanya Tilak d. Justice Ranade
explanation: The verified answer here is option B (Lokmanya Tilak). Tilak helped shape the Deccan Education Society milieu, launched anti-cow-killing leagues, akhadas and lathi clubs, and preached active defiance — the profile matches him, not Naoroji, Gokhale or Ranade alone.

subject: History
question: Name my bull “Britannia”, name my favorite horse “Turkish Flage”, name my guard “Japan”, therefore would it be right for me to become the leader of Japan or Turkey ? Who made this statement in A.D. 1920 regarding the candidacy of Bombay Legislature ?
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj used this biting analogy in 1920 to reject the idea that adopting Western names or symbols made one fit to lead foreign peoples — a sharp comment on Bombay Legislature candidacy and colonial mimicry.

subject: Geography
question: Konkan coastline belongs to which of the following type ?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. The Konkan coast is a submerged (drowned) coastline where river mouths widen into estuaries — the classic Ria type. Fiord needs glacial valleys; Dalmatian needs offshore islands parallel to the coast.

subject: History
question: 'The Hindu Mahasabha did not in any way competitor to the Congress but established to supplement and strengthen the Indian National Congress.' Who among the following explained that ?
explanation: The right pick is option D. Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya maintained that the Hindu Mahasabha was meant to complement and strengthen the Congress, not rival it — reflecting the early cooperative vision some leaders held.

subject: General Studies
question: What is the first stage in Environmental Management Systems (EMS) process ?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. In ISO 14001-style EMS, the very first step is to establish an environmental policy — top management's written commitment before objectives, targets, or implementation plans are set.

subject: General Studies
question: In order to accelerate efforts to meet water related challenges, the United Nations General Assembly declared 2018 – 2028 decade as which of the following ?

options.A: International water decade for action on water for drinking and sanitation
options.B: International water decade for action on water and environment
options.C: International water decade for drinking water supply
options.D: International water decade for action on water for sustainable development

explanation: The examiner has marked option D. The UN General Assembly declared 2018–2028 the International Decade for Action on Water for Sustainable Development — linking water access, sanitation, and SDG targets in one framework.

subject: General Studies
question: When International Bio-diversity Conservation Day is celebrated ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. International Day for Biological Diversity is observed every year on 22 May — the date the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was adopted in 1992. Do not confuse it with World Environment Day (5 June).

subject: Geography
question: Compact or clustered settlements have the following characteristics. a. Compact or clustered settlements have been found in India in plains as well as areas with fertile soils. b. Compact settlement can also lead to negative aspects such as unsanitary conditions, social tensions, health problems etc. c. The composition of the houses in these settlements found circular. d. This type of settlement is found in hilly areas, dense forest and arid region. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct ?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Compact settlements cluster in fertile plains where farming is easy (a), and high density can bring sanitation and health pressures (b). Per the official key, d is also counted here — revise compact vs dispersed settlement types together.

subject: Geography
question: In which district is Surjagad iron ore field is located ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Surjagad iron ore field lies in Gadchiroli district of eastern Maharashtra, in the Surjagad hills near Etapalli tehsil. It is a well-known iron ore belt in the Gadchiroli–Chandrapur mineral zone.

subject: Geography
question: Match the following. a. Koyna - I. 1991 b. Killari - II. 1967 c. Bhuj - III. 1993 d. Uttar Kashi - IV. 2001
explanation: The right pick is option B. Koyna shook in 1967, Killari (Latur) in 1993, Bhuj in 2001, and Uttarkashi in 1991 — so a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I. Pin these four dates; they recur often in Maharashtra geography papers.

subject: Science
question: The radiation from a radioactive sample is allowed to pass through a magnetic field region. Which of the following statement is correct ?

options.A: All the radiation get deflected in only one direction
options.C: The radiation splits into three components and follows random path
options.D: The radiation splits into three different components, two bending in opposite directions and the third remain undeflected

explanation: The examiner has marked option D. When radioactive emissions pass through a magnetic field, they split into three beams: α-particles bend one way, β-particles the opposite way, and γ-rays pass straight through undeflected.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following mountain range is on the northern boarder of Maharashtra ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The Satpura range forms Maharashtra's northern boundary, running east–west along the Narmada–Tapi trough. Harischandra-Balaghat and Mahadev ranges lie further south on the Deccan plateau.

subject: Geography
question: Arrange the mountain ranges spread over the Maharashtra plateau from North to South. a. Satpuda range b. Harischandra Balaghat range c. Mahadev Dongar range d. Satmala-Ajinta Dongar range
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. From north to south across the Maharashtra plateau: Satpuda (a) → Satmala-Ajanta (d) → Harischandra-Balaghat (b) → Mahadev range (c). Map this sequence once and it sticks.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following is the property of Gamma Rays ?

options.A: It carries two units of positive charge
options.B: The ionizing power is 100 times greater than beta rays
options.C: They are not affected by electric and magnetic field

explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves with zero charge, so neither electric nor magnetic fields can deflect them. Alpha carries +2 charge; beta carries −1 charge.

subject: Science
question: Match the pairs of the physical quantity and their units. i. Length ii. Mass iii. Time iv. Temperature A. Second B. Centimeter C. Gram D. Kelvin
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Length pairs with centimetre (B), mass with gram (C), time with second (A), and temperature with kelvin (D) — giving the order B, C, A, D.

subject: Science
question: Alum is used for water purification, which of the following element has maximum percentage by weight in composition of alum ? (Atomic Weight : O = 16, Al = 27, S = 32, K = 39)
explanation: The right pick is option C. Potash alum KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O has 20 oxygen atoms per formula unit (total mass 320 out of ~474), giving oxygen the highest weight percentage — well above K, Al, or S alone.

subject: Science
question: Out of the following animals of Phylum Reptilia, which is a living fossil ?
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Sphenodon (tuatara) of New Zealand is called a living fossil — it has barely changed since the Mesozoic era, unlike common lizards such as Hemidactylus, Chameleon, or Draco.

subject: Science
question: In modern periodic table, while going from left to right, in a second period from Lithium to Fluorine the atomic radius of elements goes on _________. a. Increasing b. Decreasing c. First decreases and then increases d. Stable

options.A: Only d and c are incorrect

explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Moving left to right across period 2 (Li → F), nuclear charge rises while electrons enter the same shell, so atomic radius steadily decreases — only statement b holds.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following animals belong to the same phylum ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Octopus, Pila (apple snail), and Sepia (cuttlefish) all belong to Phylum Mollusca. Asterias is an echinoderm; Holothuria is a sea cucumber — different phyla altogether.

subject: Science
question: Who among the following Scientists is considered as a 'Father of Taxonomy' ?
explanation: The right pick is option C. Carolus Linnaeus (Carl von Linné) laid down binomial nomenclature and systematic classification — which is why he is honoured as the Father of Taxonomy. Robert Brown, Lamarck, and Hooke made other landmark contributions.

subject: General Studies
question: What is the major cause for the depletion of the ozone layer ?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine radicals in the stratosphere that destroy ozone molecules — the primary human cause taught for ozone-hole depletion. CO₂ drives warming, not direct ozone loss.

subject: Science
question: ____________ produce extreme virus resistance in transgenic plant.
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. RNA silencing (RNA interference) degrades viral RNA inside transgenic plants, giving strong virus resistance — a standard biotech tool beyond conventional breeding or hybridization.

subject: Science
question: Arrange Hierarchy of classification. a. Order b. Class c. Genus d. Family
explanation: The right pick is option C. In the standard taxonomic ladder, Class comes first, then Order, Family, and finally Genus — so the sequence is b → a → d → c. Memorise this chain: Class → Order → Family → Genus, sitting just above Species.

subject: Science
question: The __________ is plant hormone, which is responsible for closing of stomata during stress caused by water.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Abscisic acid (ABA) is the stress hormone that signals stomata to close when the plant faces water shortage, cutting transpiration loss. Auxins and gibberellins play other roles — growth and elongation — not drought-triggered stomatal closure.

subject: Geography
question: If you are studying the effect of drought on vegetation, which portion of the electromagnetic spectrum would provide the most potential data ?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Healthy vegetation strongly reflects near-infrared radiation, so drought-stressed or sparse cover shows up clearly in that band during remote sensing. Thermal and middle infrared are more useful for temperature and moisture mapping.

subject: Science
question: Consider the following statements. a. GIS is used for spatial analysis. b. GIS is used for transmission of energy from the source to the surface of the earth. c. GIS is used for data visualization. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. GIS handles spatial analysis and data visualization on maps; it does not transmit energy from a source to Earth's surface — that description belongs to remote sensing platforms, not GIS software.

subject: Geography
question: Which type of aerial photograph has the equal scale of the entire aerial photograph ?
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. A vertical aerial photograph is taken looking straight down, so scale stays nearly uniform across the entire frame. Oblique shots tilt the camera, stretching scale from foreground to background.

subject: Science
question: Why is secondary memory necessary in a computer system ?

options.A: To provide faster data access compared to RAM
options.B: To store data and programs permanently

explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. RAM is volatile — it loses data when power goes off. Secondary memory (hard disk, SSD) stores programs and files permanently so they survive shutdown and can be reloaded later.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following detects the syntax errors and report them to the programmers ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. A compiler scans your source code for syntax errors — wrong keywords, missing semicolons, and the like — before producing machine code. The operating system manages hardware; it does not check program grammar.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following is not an example of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) model of cloud computing ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. AWS EC2, Azure VM, and Google Compute Engine rent virtual servers — classic IaaS. GitHub is a code-hosting and collaboration platform; it does not provision raw compute infrastructure.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following device is used as input as well as output device ?
explanation: The right pick is option C. A touch screen accepts finger input and simultaneously displays output on the same surface. A touch pad and mouse are input-only; a CRT monitor is output-only.

subject: Economy
question: Bulk imports are divided into which of the following three components ? a. Mineral oil, crude oil and products etc. b. Bulk consumption goods which comprise of cereals and pulses, edible oils and sugar etc. c. Capital goods, metals, machine tools, electrical and non-electrical machinery etc. d. Fertilizers, non-ferrous metals, paper and paper boards, iron and steel etc.
explanation: The right pick is option B. Bulk imports in India are grouped into three heads: petroleum and mineral oil, bulk consumption goods (cereals, pulses, edible oils, sugar), and intermediate goods like fertilisers, non-ferrous metals, and iron and steel. Capital goods form a separate category.

subject: Economy
question: Almost 93 to 94 per cent foreign aid over the entire period of 1951-52 to 2018-19 has been received in the form of ________ to India.
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Over 1951-52 to 2018-19, roughly 93–94% of India's foreign aid arrived as loans rather than outright grants. Aid packages were predominantly credit-based, with grants forming a small share.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct ? i. Nineteen banks were nationalised in the year 1969. ii. Commercial Banks with deposits worth more than Rs. 50 crore, were nationalised.
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. In July 1969, fourteen commercial banks — not nineteen — with deposits exceeding ₹50 crore were nationalised. Statement ii captures that deposit threshold correctly; statement i gets the count wrong.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following points shows failure of economic reforms in its evaluation ? a. Jobless growth b. Increasing inequalities c. Increasing economic growth rate d. Reduced public expenditure on health services Choose correct option from the following.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Jobless growth, rising inequality, and shrinking public health spending are cited as reform shortcomings. A higher GDP growth rate (c) is generally counted as a success, not a failure.

subject: Economy
question: The share of Gender Budget allocation in the current Union Budget has increased to _______ in F.Y. 2025-26 from 6.8% in F.Y. 2024-25.
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. In Union Budget 2025-26, the Gender Budget's share of total allocation rose to 8.86%, up from 6.8% in 2024-25. Track these budget headline figures for current-affairs questions.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following equation of exchange explains Fisher's quantity theory of money ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Fisher's quantity theory rests on the equation of exchange MV = PT, linking money supply (M), velocity (V), price level (P), and transactions (T). The other options rearrange terms incorrectly.

subject: Polity
question: Match the Finance Commission and its Chairman correctly. a. Thirteenth Finance Commission b. Fourteenth Finance Commission c. Fifteenth Finance Commission d. Sixteenth Finance Commission i. Arvind Pangariya ii. N. K. Singh iii. Vijay Kelkar iv. Y. V. Reddy
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Vijay Kelkar chaired the 13th Finance Commission, Y. V. Reddy the 14th, N. K. Singh the 15th, and Arvind Panagariya heads the 16th — matching a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following credit rating agencies is not registered with SEBI in India ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Moody's is a US-based global agency and is not registered with SEBI as a credit rating agency in India. CARE, CRISIL, and Brickwork Ratings are domestically registered.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which of the following country/ies is/are not a member of ASEAN ? a. Philippines b. Cambodia c. Indonesia d. India
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. ASEAN has ten Southeast Asian members including the Philippines, Cambodia, and Indonesia. India is not a member; it engages with ASEAN as a dialogue partner.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is not included in competitive federalism adopted by Niti Ayog ? a. Encouraging healthy competition among States for State ranking. b. School education and health index of States. c. Export competitiveness index of States. d. Security market index. Choose correct answer.
explanation: The right pick is option D. NITI Aayog's competitive federalism framework ranks states on education, health, and export competitiveness indices. A security market index is not part of this state-ranking exercise.

subject: Reasoning

question: 39. भारताच्या भूभागातील सामाजिक आणि शैक्षणिक दृष्ट्या मागासवर्गीयांच्या स्थितीची चौकशी करण्यासाठी आयोग नियुक्त करण्याचा अधिकार संविधानाच्या कोणत्या कलमाद्वारे राष्ट्रपतींना देण्यात आला आहे ?
explanation: येथे खरे उत्तर पर्याय B. कलम 340 राष्ट्रपतींना सामाजिक व शैक्षणिक दृष्ट्या मागास वर्गांची स्थिती तपासण्यासाठी आयोग नियुक्त करण्याचा अधिकार देते. कलम 342 मागास वर्ग निश्चित करण्याशी संबंधित आहे, चौकशी आयोग नियुक्त करण्याशी नाही.

subject: Reasoning
question: 30. 30% विद्यार्थी सकाळ वृत्तपत्र वाचतात आणि 40% विद्यार्थी लोकमत वृत्तपत्र वाचतात, जर 15% विद्यार्थी दोन्ही वृत्तपत्र वाचत असतील तर किती टक्के विद्यार्थी कुठलेच वृत्तपत्र वाचत नाहीत ?
explanation: अधिकृत उत्तर पर्याय C. किमान एक वृत्तपत्र वाचणारे = 30 + 40 − 15 = 55%, म्हणून कुठलेही न वाचणारे = 100 − 55 = 45%. दोन गटांच्या छेदनासाठी समावेश-वगळ या सूत्राचा वापर करा.

question: कायद्यासमोर समानता या नियमासाठी खालीलपैकी कोणते अपवाद आहेत ? अ. राष्ट्रपती किंवा राज्यपाल हे त्यांच्या पदाचे अधिकार व कार्य निर्वहनासाठी कोणत्याही न्यायालयाला जबाबदार नसतात. ब. परदेशी सार्वभौम, राजदूत व राजनैतिक अधिकारी यांना दिवाणी व फौजदारी कारवाईपासून मुक्तता मिळते. क. संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघटना व त्याची अभिकरणे यांना राजनैतिक विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त आहेत.
explanation: अधिकृत उत्तर पर्याय D आहे. कलम 14 मधील कायद्यासमोर समानता या तत्त्वाला अपवाद आहेत — राष्ट्रपती/राज्यपालांची अधिकृत कार्यांसाठी न्यायालयीन जबाबदारी नसणे, परदेशी सार्वभौम व राजदूतांची मुक्तता, आणि संयुक्त राष्ट्र व त्याच्या अभिकरणांचे विशेषाधिकार. तिन्ही विधाने योग्य आहेत.
